rv.q: If Chiaroscuro occasionally falters under the weight of its ambition, it ultimately dazzles with its daring.

There’s gentle provocation and some subtle amusement in the individual vignettes that build to an absurdist climax, but, taken all at once, the play would have benefited from a tightening and trimming that its production history rendered impossible.

cn.t: Critics praise this world premiere of Aishah Rahman's nautical comedy, with the National Black Theatre production earning acclaim for bringing the late playwright's unproduced work to vibrant life under abigail jean-baptiste's direction.
